coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.note: Coverage counts the entries for which a method gave a label, over the whole corpus of the run. A method that abstained and a method that failed technically are counted separately.
coverage.caption: Coverage and label distribution per method

accuracy.title: Accuracy and recall
accuracy.note: Accuracy divides the correct labels by the entries the method answered, on the benchmark only.
accuracy.effectiveNote: Effective accuracy divides by the whole benchmark, so an abstention counts against the method. This is the definition of the published study.
accuracy.recallNote: Recall per class is the share of that class the method got right, with a {level} % Wilson confidence interval in brackets, then correct / class size.
accuracy.recallNoteUnknown: Recall per class is the share of that class the method got right, with a Wilson confidence interval in brackets, then correct / class size.
accuracy.caption: Accuracy, effective accuracy and per-class recall per method

confusion.title: Confusion matrices
confusion.note: Rows are the benchmark label, columns the label the method gave. Only entries the method answered are counted.

kappa.title: Agreement between methods (Cohen’s κ)
kappa.note: Cohen’s κ is computed pairwise between methods, only on entries both answered. It measures how well two methods agree beyond chance. It is not agreement between human annotators.
kappa.undefinedNote: n/d: κ is undefined when fewer than two entries were answered by both methods, or when both methods gave one constant label.
kappa.caption: Pairwise Cohen’s κ between methods
kappa.undefined: κ is undefined for this pair

ensemble.title: Ensemble
ensemble.none: This evaluation was started without an aggregation, so there are no ensemble figures.
ensemble.note: How the chosen aggregation decided over the whole run, and how much of it people have reviewed.
ensemble.review: {reviewed} people were reviewed by a human, {corrected} of them were corrected.

export.title: Exports
export.intro: An export writes the result of one completed aggregation out of the system: the source TEI files with the labels written back, a JSON result bundle or a CSV report. It is a stored, reproducible result, and a manifest records the checksums of what it produced and the source it started from.
export.forbidden: Only project operators can start an export. You can read and download the exports below.
export.empty: No export has been started on this run yet.
export.loadError: The exports could not be loaded.

new.title: Start an export
new.noAggregation: An export needs a completed aggregation. Create one on the run first.

formats.tei: TEI: the source files with the labels written back

new.teiNotPossible: A TEI export needs a dataset imported from one TEI file or several loose TEI files. This run’s dataset does not meet that requirement.

policies.machine: the machine’s aggregated decision for everybody
policies.human: the human decision where somebody reviewed a person, the machine’s otherwise

new.policyHint: Neither choice changes a stored prediction or aggregated result; it only picks which decision is written out.

detail.downloadNote: Downloading also computes the SHA-256 checksum of the bytes that arrived. Compare it with the checksum recorded for this output in the export’s manifest.json.
detail.manifestReceived: This export produced several outputs, so the download is its manifest; the outputs are listed in the manifest section above and are not downloadable separately.
detail.verifyLabel: Checksum from the manifest (paste it to compare)

manifest.title: Manifest
manifest.note: The server records this manifest when the export completes; it does not change afterwards.

manifestVerdict.notApplicable: This download is the manifest itself, so there is no output to compare it to.
